headline: Australia targets tech giants with fines up to five percent of global revenue
label: NEWS
caption:
Australia is cracking down on Big Tech with massive financial penalties for online harm 🇦🇺

According to Al Jazeera, Australia has announced plans to fine tech companies up to five percent of their worldwide revenue if they fail to remove harmful content from their platforms. Companies like Google and Meta could face these penalties under a new digital duty of care law detailed by the government.

Communications Minister Anika Wells told reporters that the legislation is seismic and urgent reform. The bill is expected to be approved in Parliament this week after being agreed upon by the Labor government and the Greens.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told Parliament that the law puts parents and children first over foreign owned tech companies. The legislation also gives individuals the right to sue platforms for enabling wrongdoing and allows users aged 16 or older to turn off algorithm driven feeds.

Industry groups have opposed the bill on the grounds that it gives government officials discretion to decide what counts as harmful content. Targeted harms include child s*xual ab*se material, nonconsensual fake n*de material, gender based violence, self harm promotion and terrorism.
